summary: The milestone completed 7 experiments in 1.2 minutes, with 2 marked compute-bound. The longest listed item was the 0.97-minute synthesis-only freshness receipt; the longest named compute-bound item took 0.16 minutes. The locked task-conditioned indicator reports no compute-bound GPU idle, but task-time utilization efficiency cannot be established from the monitor snapshot.
bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only freshness receipt was the largest observed elapsed item, making incremental freshness handling the clearest recorded throughput opportunity.
Disk-modification-time reconstruction does not separate queueing, setup, inference, or teardown, so the cause of the named compute-bound duration is unavailable.
The bounded slowest list names only one compute-bound item even though the locked count shows two; the other compute path cannot be ranked or diagnosed from the supplied evidence.
No task-level model-concurrency or runner-selection evidence is available, so a missed DualGPURunner engagement cannot be identified.
improvements_suggested: Cache freshness inputs by content and reuse unchanged literature and implementation receipts.
Write monotonic phase timings directly into each experiment artifact instead of depending on disk modification times.
Attach task-scoped GPU samples, declared model count, and selected runner to each compute artifact; use DualGPURunner only for parallel multi-model loads.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add content-addressed reuse to the freshness-receipt path.
Persist phase-level timing receipts with every experiment result.
Record model concurrency, runner choice, and task-correlated GPU telemetry for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports better timing and concurrency observability plus freshness-receipt reuse, but it does not support a nonzero savings forecast because no measured faster path is supplied. The idle monitor snapshot is not assigned to compute execution because the locked task-conditioned field is false.
